title: Dead man's relatives sue police, doctors
article: The family of a man who died in hospital after being arrested by Windsor police is seeking $1.75 million in a lawsuit against the force, the officers involved, the hospital and the doctors who treated him.
Bryan Dukic, 42, died in Hotel-Dieu Grace Hospital on April 5, 2006, within three hours of being detained by police behind a west side apartment complex.

An investigation by the province's Special Investigations Unit cleared the officers involved of wrongdoing. There was a subsequent inquest, but under the Coroners Act jurors aren't allowed to appropriate blame. One of its recommendations was for police to receive better training.
Lawyer Gino Morga, who is representing Dukic's mother Anna and his siblings, said the suit is aimed at restitution for the family and assigning some blame for his death.
"I think the major problem here is the conduct of the police, and the amount of contribution by the other entities may be large, may be small, and that will be determined by the courts," said Morga.

The suit is seeking $250,000 in general damages "for the pain and suffering of the late Bryan Dukic," damages under the Family Law Act for $500,000, and punitive, aggravated or exemplary damages in the amount of $1 million.
Morga was reluctant to discuss money and said it is not the real issue.
"I'm just looking for fair restitution for my client," said Morga. "Unfortunately, money is the only form of restitution. They don't do resurrections anymore."

The lawsuit names Windsor police constables John Ryan and Richard Sieberer, Windsor police, Dukic's family physician Dr. Jairie Ferasol, Hotel-Dieu Grace Hospital and hospital emergency room physician Dr. Gordon Vail.

The statement of claim -- which contains allegations not proven in court -- says that during Dukic's arrest for driving while disqualified Ryan and Sieberer "applied physical force including throwing Bryan to the ground, kneeing or kicking him, punching him and dragging him along the ground."
At the inquest the jury ruled Dukic's death an accident caused by massive internal bleeding from lacerations to the spleen, made worse by liver cirrhosis and trauma to the chest wall.
The suit also claims the officers knew Dukic suffered from liver problems and when he was expressing pain to his ribs the officers failed to take measures for medical assistance.
The suit also claims Ferasol, the family doctor, failed to appropriately test Dukic for his problems and the hospital and Vail failed to diagnose his condition or perform emergency surgery.
A statement of defence on behalf of the doctors and hospital said that Dukic was seen by Ferasol a number of times in the months before his death.

Dukic was notified of various problems but stopped seeing the doctor after March 10, 2006. "Dr. Ferasol reminded Mr. Dukic that it was important for him to stop drinking alcohol, as the Hepatitis C virus and drinking would hasten his liver disease," the statement reads.
An intent to defend has been filed by Windsor police but the full statement has not been submitted.
